text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-U.S. official Pelletro said the "Friends of Lebanon" meeting, to be held in Washington on December 16 for countries interested in giving Lebanon financial assistance for postwar reconstruction, will be successful.
-The government gives permission to two private television stations to start broadcasting via satellite, one of them is owned by Prime Minister Hariri.
-Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce completed a $60-million capital increase through the first simultaneous local and international share offering by a Lebanese issuer.
-The draft of lifting a U.S. travel ban on Lebanon is ready.
-Parliament Speaker Berri will head to Damascus today to meet Syrian President Assad.
-The Council of Maronite Bishops said the Taif agreement, which ended the civil war, needs many amendments.
-Agriculture Minister Fakhoury says: "We will ask for $1.6 million from the 'Friends of Lebanon' meeting to finance water projects."
